sources.ref_file_title: HN24 - One-Way Functions and Zero Knowledge
sources.note: Also ECCC TR24-063 (https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2024/063/). Proves: a one-way function exists iff NP is contained in CZK and NP is hard in the worst case - i.e. removes OW93's auxiliary-input relaxation for NP.

sources.ref_file_title: Ost91 - One-way functions, hard on average problems, and statistical zero-knowledge proofs
sources.note: Precursor rather than follow-up: the statistical-ZK, hard-on-average case with a standard (not auxiliary-input) one-way function as conclusion. Already a reference page in the wiki; listed here so the improvements bullet resolves.

pages.class_justification: OW93 builds the candidate one-way function out of the proof system's simulator and concludes auxiliary-input one-wayness; the paper does not classify the reduction, and none of the RTV04 notions is evidenced by the construction shape. Guessing fully-black-box here would assert something the source does not support, so the honest value is `unstated`.
pages.model_justification: Plain model. The proof system, its simulator, and the resulting one-way function all live in the standard model; the claim is explicitly 'in the plain model'.
pages.statement: If a language outside $\classBPP$ has a computational [[zero-knowledge-proof|zero-knowledge proof]], then auxiliary-input one-way functions exist; equivalently, if auxiliary-input one-way functions do not exist, then every language with a zero-knowledge proof lies in $\classBPP$. When the language is instead hard on average, the conclusion strengthens to a standard [[hash-function|one-way function]] — [[OW93 - One-way functions are essential for non-trivial zero-knowledge|OW93]].
pages.sketch: The candidate one-way function is read off the zero-knowledge simulator: an algorithm that inverts the simulator's output distribution is turned into a distinguisher that decides the language, so a language outside $\classBPP$ forces the function to be hard to invert (in the auxiliary-input sense).
pages.improvements_text:
- Under worst-case hardness of $\classNP$ the auxiliary-input relaxation is unnecessary: a one-way function exists if and only if $\classNP \subseteq \classCZK$ and $\classNP$ is hard in the worst case — [[HN24 - One-Way Functions and Zero Knowledge|HN24]]
- The statistical-zero-knowledge case, giving a standard one-way function from a hard-on-average language, predates OW93 — [[Ost91 - One-way functions, hard on average problems, and statistical zero-knowledge proofs|Ost91]]
notes_to_keep: The conclusion node is `hash-function`, which the wiki also uses for collision-resistant hashing; only the one-wayness variant is meant here.

The hyperedge's `hypotheses: [zkp]` cannot carry OW93's non-triviality qualifier (the proved language must lie outside $\classBPP$, or be hard on average for the standard-OWF conclusion); the qualifier survives only in the statement prose.
flags: zkp-to-hash-function: `source: folklore` is wrong and the page's own Notes already say so — this is the Ostrovsky-Wigderson theorem. Replace with OW93.

zkp-to-hash-function: LOAD-BEARING QUALIFIER MISSING FROM THE EDGE. The migrated claim 'ZK proofs for NP imply OWF' is false as literally stated: if P = NP then every language has a trivial ZK proof and no OWF exists. The theorem needs non-triviality (language outside BPP) or average-case hardness. I kept the edge and repaired the statement; a human should decide whether the hyperedge format should instead carry a second hypothesis node for the hardness condition.

zkp-to-hash-function: OW93's conclusion is an AUXILIARY-INPUT one-way function, a weaker object than the wiki's `hash-function`/OWF node. Only the average-case variant (or HN24 under worst-case NP hardness) yields a standard OWF. The conclusion node overstates the theorem as encoded.

notes_to_keep: Fiat-Shamir applies only to public-coin, constant-round (sigma) protocols with negligible or amplified soundness error, and is insecure for general interactive proofs — [[GK03 - On the (In)security of the Fiat-Shamir Paradigm|GK03]].
BFM88 does not compile an arbitrary zero-knowledge proof: it constructs NIZK for NP in the CRS model from trapdoor permutations, so the assumption hypothesis is missing from any edge that drops it.
pages.wrong_reason: As encoded — `hypotheses: [zkp]`, `conclusion: nizk`, `model: standard` — this page asserts that interactive zero-knowledge proofs yield non-interactive ones in the plain model. That is false: a plain-model NIZK proof system exists only for languages in $\classBPP$ (Goldreich-Oren, J. Cryptology 7(1):1-32, 1994, DOI 10.1007/BF00195207), so no setup-free compiler can exist for a non-trivial language. Both citations the page carries are setup-dependent, and both branches already exist as their own pages: the Fiat-Shamir branch (public-coin constant-round protocol, random-oracle model, FS86) is `red-rom-and-zkp-to-nizk-fs86`, and the CRS branch is `red-tdp-to-nizk-bfm88`, where BFM88 builds NIZK for NP from trapdoor permutations in the CRS model rather than compiling an arbitrary ZK proof. This page is those two edges with the setup dropped; the correct action is to delete it (or merge it into `red-rom-and-zkp-to-nizk-fs86`, which is the same slug suffix and the same claim stated in the right model).

pages.class_justification: A proven containment between complexity classes, established by a direct simulation argument with no restriction on technique. `free` is this repo's recorded convention for such inclusions and matches the sibling pages `red-p-to-zpp` and `red-rp-to-bpp`.
pages.statement: Every language decided by a zero-error probabilistic polynomial-time machine — a machine of [[zero-error-probabilistic-polynomial-time|ZPP]] — is decided by a probabilistic polynomial-time machine with one-sided error, so $\classZPP \subseteq \classRP$ and [[randomized-polynomial-time|RP]] contains ZPP. This is one half of the identity $\classZPP = \classRP \cap \mathbf{coRP}$ — folklore.
pages.sketch: Run the Las Vegas machine for $2p(n)$ steps, where $p$ bounds its expected running time; by Markov's inequality it halts within that budget with probability at least $1/2$, and whenever it halts its answer is correct. Rejecting on timeout therefore never accepts a no-instance and accepts a yes-instance with probability at least $1/2$, which is exactly the $\classRP$ condition.
flags: zpp-to-rp: the statement keeps the wikilinks in prose and the containment in math (`$\classZPP \subseteq \classRP$`), since wikilinks inside `$...$` do not render. Reword freely, but do not move the links into the math.

zpp-to-rp: class `free` was already set correctly by the migration and the existing Notes justify it; only the boilerplate `class: unstated` paragraph (which contradicts the frontmatter) should be dropped.

zpp-to-rp: EDITOR LANE, other pages - `content/Complexity/zero-error-probabilistic-polynomial-time.md` and `content/Complexity/bounded-error-probabilistic-polynomial-time.md` state the chain $\classP \subseteq \classZPP \subseteq \classRP \subseteq \classBPP$ with the class macros only and no wikilinks or `— standard` label. Same defect noted on `red-p-to-zpp` and `red-rp-to-bpp`.

zpp-to-rp: no citation proposed. The classes are due to Gill (SICOMP 1977) and the containment is immediate from the definitions plus Markov, so it is textbook/folklore rather than an attributable theorem; I deliberately did not add Gill77 as an `original` source.
